payload.how: every adapter's example runs against the real admin, `examples/payload-backend`, in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit
the protocol watch runs `@payloadcms/live-preview@latest` against the captured messages, and the real-admin suite against `payload@latest`
the same against `@payloadcms/live-preview@beta` and `payload@beta`; a failure there warns and does not gate a release

on 2026-11-02, the 7 cases of `tests/real-payload/surface-findings.spec.ts` passed in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit against the admin fixture with beta.6 installed over it (Node 24.22.1); an upload reached an `` inside a `` through the REST merge, and a Lexical edit was written by the client-side renderer, internal link included. Relationships were not part of the run

on 2026-10-24, in a consumer project on 2.1.0 (Next.js 16, Node 24), the config plugin type-checked against Payload's declarations and passed its config sanitizing; for six documents in two locales it built the URL a hand-written callback produced, apart from the order of the query parameters, and the locale reached the path resolvers; the `payload-session` strategy authorized against an admin with a `csrf` list once its `origin` option was set. Globals, the create screen, drafts and autosave, other plugins that write a Live Preview URL and replacing breakpoints were not part of the run

on 2026-10-26, a 2.2 release candidate on a consumer site: typing into a title and a text line patched the preview, typing into a rich-text field updated it through 7 fragment renders that answered 200, the frame never reloaded, and all 31 messages had the shape of the captured ones. Relationships and uploads were not part of the run

the [local release checks](testing.md#local-release-checks) drive the real admin in DOM, React and Vue previews, in frontend-only and `serverURL` modes (24 browser cases per variant), and take the React hook and the Vue composable through three lifecycle journeys (9 browser cases per variant) and seven guard journeys (21 browser cases per variant) in development builds; the Payload 2 dependency graph retains upstream audit findings

vite.devBelowNewest: 2026-09-06: the devDependency stays at Vite 7 because @codspeed/vitest-plugin peers on ^4 || ^5 || ^6 || ^7, and raising it made npm ci fail with ERESOLVE — every CI job stopped before its first test. It decides only which Vite the repository's own tools run against; the supported majors are the rows above, and the fixtures install 5 through 8. Remove this line when the dev tooling accepts 8.
